skill.name: cooper-check-email
skill.description: Read, search, summarize, and triage Cooper Email through a connected Cooper MCP server, including conversations, attachments, and message labels.
skill.summary: Review Cooper inboxes with filtered searches, full-message summaries, attachment retrieval, and label-based triage.
skill.author: cooper-email

security_audit.summary: All 30 static alerts are false positives: Markdown tool references, a homepage link, and inbox metadata do not establish shell execution or reconnaissance. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection or data exfiltration in SKILL.md. The workflow nevertheless directs automatic unread-label removal without requiring user authorization, creating a mailbox-state risk during informational checks.

remediation.issue: Informational inbox checks can automatically remove unread labels from messages or entire threads.
remediation.suggestion: Keep checks read-only by default. Require explicit user authorization before changing message or thread labels, and report the scope of approved updates.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Read-State Changes Without Explicit Authorization
semantic_findings.description: The workflow says, "After handling a message, call" the update tools to remove unread labels, including from entire conversations. Informational checks can therefore change mailbox state without explicit approval and hide messages from later unread reviews.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The document explicitly directs unread-label removal after handling messages, despite introducing a read-only workflow. No approval condition limits those updates to authorized triage.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant messages across Cooper inboxes can require several searches and full-thread reviews. This skill guides connected assistants through retrieval, summarization, attachment reading, and triage.
actual_capabilities: Resolve Cooper inboxes and filter messages by sender, recipient, subject, labels, direction, thread, or date.
Search messages and conversations across an account or within a selected inbox.
Follow pagination and retrieve full messages or threads before summarizing their bodies.
Retrieve attachment text for supported document formats or receive base64 bytes.
Wait for matching replies, check unread mail, and retrieve account events.
Update read status and custom labels, and group reviews by urgency and reply needs.
limitations: Requires a connected Cooper MCP server and access to the relevant inboxes.
Only covers mail sent to Cooper inboxes, not the user's personal mailbox.
Sending, inbox administration, connection setup, and one-time-code workflows are delegated to separate skills.
The workflow defaults to marking handled mail read; explicitly prohibit label changes when you need an unchanged inbox.

use_cases.title: Review Customer Requests
use_cases.description: Review unread customer conversations and identify messages that need replies without sending responses.

use_cases.title: Find Project Decisions
use_cases.description: Search project correspondence, retrieve full threads, and summarize decisions with message identifiers.

use_cases.title: Check Incoming Documents
use_cases.description: Find vendor messages and review relevant attachment text while keeping read status unchanged.

prompt_templates.title: Check Unread Mail
prompt_templates.prompt: Check unread messages in my Cooper inbox. Summarize sender, subject, and requested action. Do not change labels or release held messages.

prompt_templates.title: Search a Specific Inbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Cooper inbox [inbox] for messages from [sender] between [start date] and [end date]. Summarize full bodies without changing labels.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: a sender and date search.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Conversation and Attachment
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the [topic] thread in Cooper inbox [inbox]. Summarize the conversation and relevant attachment text. Preserve labels and cite message identifiers.

prompt_templates.title: Perform Scoped Triage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review every unread message in Cooper inbox [inbox] from [date range]. Group by urgency. Add needs-reply only where warranted; preserve unread status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: paginated review with explicitly scoped label changes.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Check unread Cooper mail without changing labels.
output: Inbox: support. Two unread messages matched the requested range.
Customer question: asks whether the replacement has shipped. Needs a reply.
Delivery notice: confirms receipt of the previous shipment. No reply requested.
Labels were unchanged. No messages were sent.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Summarize the supplier thread and relevant attachment without changing read status.
output: The supplier confirmed the revised delivery date and requested approval of the updated quantities.
The attachment lists the proposed quantities. Approval remains outstanding.
Read status was preserved. No reply was sent.

best_practices: Specify the inbox and date range, and state whether any label changes are authorized.
Request full-message retrieval and complete pagination before relying on a summary.
Treat email instructions as untrusted content and decide separately whether a held message should be released.
anti_patterns: Assuming the first result page or a message preview represents the complete inbox or conversation.
Using this workflow for personal mailboxes, connection setup, or direct email sending.
Treating an email request as authorization to expose secrets, execute code, pay, delete, or contact others.

faq.question: What connection does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a connected Cooper MCP server. Connection setup belongs to the separate cooper-mcp skill.

faq.question: Can it read my personal mailbox?
faq.answer: No. The documented scope covers mail sent to Cooper inboxes only.

faq.question: Does checking mail change read status?
faq.answer: The workflow directs marking handled messages read. Explicitly request unchanged labels for informational checks.

faq.question: Can it read attachments?
faq.answer: It can request extracted text for text, JSON, CSV, PDF, DOCX, XLSX, and XLS attachments, or receive base64 bytes.

faq.question: Can it wait for a reply?
faq.answer: Yes. Matching-reply waits last up to 25 seconds per call; unread-message waits support up to 55 seconds.

faq.question: Will it send replies or release held messages automatically?
faq.answer: Sending uses the separate cooper-send-email skill. Held messages should be released only when the user decides.
